title: How a Naked Mole-Rat Queen's Scent Keeps the Peace
summary:
Naked mole-rats live in colonies and work together. But they can also fight fiercely. Scientists recently found that a queen keeps her colony calm with a special scent.

In a colony, some mole-rats look for food and others care for the young. Only the queen has babies. When a queen dies, high-ranking mole-rats begin mating and fight hard until one becomes the new queen.

Gary Lewin is a neuroscientist in Berlin, Germany. His team found one chemical made only by queens. It is called isopropyl myristate. The team removed a queen from her colony. Then they put the chemical on the colony every day for three months. "In the entire three months, there was no fighting," Lewin said. When the researchers stopped adding the scent, the mole-rats began to fight. Within a few weeks, a new queen emerged.

The chemical also changes hormones in female mole-rats. The queen makes it only when she is pregnant or getting ready to be. The team shared its findings on July 15 in the journal Nature.
why_it_matters: The study shows how animals can use chemicals to keep order in a group, which helps scientists understand how living things work together.
